title: Make.com for Small Business: Is It Worth Using in 2026? - InclusiveAIHub

facts.fact: According to this review, Make.com was originally launched as Integromat, was acquired by Celonis in 2020, and was rebranded to Make in 2022.
facts.quote: Originally launched as Integromat, the platform was acquired by Celonis (an enterprise process-intelligence company) in 2020 and rebranded to Make in 2022.

facts.fact: The reviewer states that Make.com connects 3,000+ applications.
facts.quote: It now connects 3,000+ applications and is used by hundreds of thousands of businesses worldwide

facts.fact: The reviewer lists the Make.com Free plan at $0 per month with 1,000 monthly operations.
facts.unit: USD per month; operations per month

facts.fact: The reviewer lists the Make.com Core plan at approximately $9 per month on an annual basis, with 10,000 monthly operations.
The reviewer lists the Make.com Pro plan at approximately $16 per month on an annual basis, with 10,000 monthly operations plus priority execution.
The reviewer lists the Make.com Teams plan at approximately $29 per month on an annual basis, with 10,000 monthly operations plus collaboration features.
The reviewer states that the Make.com Enterprise plan is priced by custom quote rather than a published rate.
The reviewer states that Make.com offers a free-forever tier plus four paid tiers.
facts.quote: Make.com uses a free-forever tier plus four paid tiers, priced by monthly operations rather than purely by seat count at the lower tiers.

facts.fact: The reviewer says pricing shown reflects typical published rates as of 2026 and that users should confirm current pricing on Make.com's official pricing page.
facts.quote: Pricing below reflects typical published rates as of 2026 — always confirm current pricing on Make.com’s official pricing page

facts.fact: The reviewer states that each individual action inside a scenario, such as a read, write, or update, typically counts as one operation.
facts.quote: each individual action inside a scenario (a read, a write, an update) typically counts as one operation.
